name: cloud-superapp
description: Diego's Cloud SuperApp — modularized monolith Android app. Single APK, gradle multi-module: app/ (launcher shell) + libs/{core,mail,cal,feed,net,ops,vault,chat}/ (independent feature modules). FairEmail-derived mail with JMAP, CalDAV/Radicale calendar, RSS, WireGuard tunnel, cloud ops dashboard, vault. Build via Nix devShell (gradle + AGP + Android SDK), one APK out.

android._doc_abi_filters: Native-library ABIs shipped in the APK. Defaults to arm64-v8a only because MapLibre Native (added in Push 2) ships ~15-18MB of .so per ABI; shipping all 4 default ABIs (arm64-v8a + armeabi-v7a + x86 + x86_64) inflates the APK from ~22MB to ~82MB. Every Samsung Galaxy from S8 (2017) onward + every modern Pixel is arm64, so this is safe for the user's device. To support 32-bit devices or x86 emulators, add 'armeabi-v7a' / 'x86_64' to this list and rebuild — no Kotlin / gradle edits needed.

toolchain._doc: Pinned for reproducibility — all derived in flake.nix. Bump here, rebuild devShell.
toolchain._doc_sdk_bump: compile_sdk bumped 34→35 to satisfy androidx.health.connect:connect-client:1.1.0-alpha10's AAR metadata constraint (it requires consumers to compile against Android 35+ for the new HC permission definitions wired to API 35 constants). AGP 8.5.2 maxes at compileSdk 34, so AGP bumped 8.5.2→8.7.3 (first stable AGP supporting compileSdk 35). Gradle 8.7→8.10.2 follows AGP 8.7's Gradle 8.9+ requirement. target_sdk stays at 34 — opting into Android 15 runtime behaviour is a separate concern from compiling against its APIs.

upstreams._doc: Workspace tracking clones of upstream FOSS apps. Each lives at ../ea_<domain>-<project>/ (gitignored, see 1_workflows/src/gitignore ea_*-*/ rule). Refresh with `git -C ../ea_<x>-<y> pull`. Code is cherry-picked into libs/<domain>/ — NEVER built as a gradle subproject directly (they're top-level apps, not libraries).

kde-connect._doc_phase: SLICE first: libs/kde-connect currently ships the wg0-preferred discovery of the Surface (ui.kde_connect) + the Configs KDE page, NOT the full upstream. Vendoring the full kdeconnect-android source (TLS pairing + plugins, whole APK -> GPL-2.0) is the documented next phase, cherry-picked into libs/kde-connect from this tracker clone.

ops._doc_no_upstream: ops is a thin c3-api dashboard — no FOSS upstream to fork. Will be original code.

core._doc_no_upstream: core is shared infra (DB, theming, prefs, the updater) — original code.

modules._doc: Single source of truth for the Gradle module graph. settings.gradle iterates this list. Adding a new feature module = one entry here + mkdir + minimal build.gradle.

app.comment: Launcher / shell. Hosts navigation to each feature module.

libs:core.comment: Shared models, DB, theming, prefs, auth. No domain logic.

libs:updater.comment: In-app auto-updater. Periodic WorkManager check against ghcr.io via OCI HTTP API (same flow build.sh phone-install uses). If remote sha256 differs from current PackageInfo's, prompts user via PackageInstaller. All knobs in release.auto_update — no hardcoded URLs.

libs:mail.comment: Mail — FairEmail-derived, JMAP-extended. Source upstream: github.com/M66B/FairEmail (GPLv3). Tracking clone lives at ../ea_mail-fairmail/.

libs:ops.comment: Cloud ops dashboard — c3-api, health checks, dagu trigger, container control.

libs:vault.comment: Passwords + TOTP. Could integrate with Vaultwarden (vault.diegonmarcos.com).

libs:chat.comment: Chat / messaging. Likely integrates with mattermost-bots (chat.diegonmarcos.com) — could fork Mattermost-Mobile / SimpleX / Conversations later.

libs:wallet.comment: Apple/Google-Wallet-style Compose surface. Cards / Tickets / Calendar / Archive tabs. Sources its vCard data from assets/qrcodes/qrcodes.json (the front repo's generated contact block). First Compose-only lib in the project — drives the kotlinCompilerExtensionVersion pin.

libs:health.comment: MyHealth — native Android Health Connect dashboard. Reads aggregated records (Steps, Distance, Floors, Elevation, HR, RHR, HRV, VO2max, BP, BloodGlucose, SpO2, Temperature, RespiratoryRate, Sleep+stages, Exercise, Weight/BodyFat/Lean/Bone/Water, Hydration, Nutrition, Cycle) via androidx.health.connect:connect-client. All of Garmin Connect / Google Fit / Samsung Health / Fitbit / Oura sync INTO Health Connect on-device — single SDK gets the union. LOCAL-ONLY: persists rollups + caches into HealthStore (libs:core, SharedPreferences). Zero network. No OAuth, no webhooks, no cloud ingester. Compose surface — pages declared in build.json::ui.sections[id=health].

libs:maps.comment: MyMaps — native GPS tracker + MapLibre Native renderer + SQLite store. Foreground LocationTrackerService writes points; StopDetector emits dwell-events; StopsEnricher resolves each Stop via the active provider (build.json::ui.maps_providers, default Nominatim public). MyTrips Dashboard + Stats read the same SQLite. All Maps* / Mytrips* / LocationTrackerService / StopsEnricher / MapsProviderClient code lives here; app/ only retains the SectionPages dispatch that imports the fragments. Native deps: org.maplibre.gl:android-sdk + play-services-location — both heavy in native .so (arm64-only via build.json::android.abi_filters).

libs:browser.comment: Browser — in-app WebView host + tab persistence. Was com.diegonmarcos.superapp.tabs in app/.../tabs/ until the libs:browser lift; renamed Tabs → Browser so the 'Tabs' namespace is free for the future App Tabs feature (last 6 opened pages/apps). BrowserHostFragment hosts the WebView in two modes — GRID (open-tab cards) and DETAIL (fullscreen WebView). BrowserTabPrefs persists the open-tabs list in SharedPreferences (file kept as 'tabs' so users' existing list survives the rename). Pulls in Collapsible / SuppressHorizontalSwipe / SuppressVerticalSwipe from libs:core (they were promoted from app/ during this lift so libs:browser doesn't back-reference app/). No native deps; WebView is part of the Android framework.

libs:fin.comment: MyFin — personal finance dashboard. Beta renders from build.json::ui.myfin_mock (accounts, monthly stats, top expense categories, recent transactions, net worth) — all data-driven so the user can iterate the layout by editing JSON without rebuilding Kotlin. Real aggregator (Plaid / GoCardless / SaltEdge / manual OFX import) lands in a follow-up. MyFinDashboardFragment is the only surface for now; pages: dashboard.

libs:apptabs.comment: App Tabs — last-6 opened SuperApp entries (sections, pages, external apps) rendered as a 2-col GRID. Sister module to libs:browser; same card-grid UX, different content (sealed Entry: SectionEntry | PageEntry | ExternalAppEntry). AppTabPrefs is SharedPreferences-backed ('app_tabs' file, strict LRU cap=6). Producers call AppTabPrefs.recordSection / recordPage / recordExternalApp on every successful navigation; the GRID re-renders on onResume so flipping back to Tabs always shows the freshest LRU. AppTabsHost is the callback interface MainActivity implements to handle card-tap re-navigation without libs:apptabs reaching back into app/.

libs:kde-connect.comment: KDE Connect integration (Configs > KDE page). SLICE, SELF-CONTAINED (no dependency on the installed org.kde.kdeconnect_tp): wg0-preferred discovery of the Surface Pro (data-driven from ui.kde_connect — wg_ip 10.0.0.5, port 1716). Binds the probe + identity socket to the native VPN (wg0) Network so packets egress the tunnel with the wg0 source IP (the peer answers to that), then the default route, then a self-contained LAN broadcast. Declared fork of github.com/KDE/kdeconnect-android (GPL-2.0, upstreams.kde-connect); full upstream TLS pairing + plugin link is the documented next phase.

ui._doc_permissions: Data-driven master list for Configs/About → Permissions. `runtime` = standard runtime-grantable Android perms (Android 6+ dangerous perms — Camera/Mic/Location/Contacts/etc.). DevControlFragment reads this list, renders one row per entry with live grant state, and bulk-requests the union via ActivityResultContracts.RequestMultiplePermissions. Special-access perms (battery whitelist, default launcher, usage stats), Health Connect perms, and System auto-granted perms are computed AT RUNTIME inside DevControlFragment — they don't need a JSON list because they're either single-flag toggles or PackageManager-introspected sets.
ui._doc: Navigation taxonomy — data-driven source for MainActivity's BottomNavigationView (bottom buttons), DrawerLayout (left-side collapsable 2-level menu), and per-section Toolbar menus. Adding a new section = one entry here + one drawable + one fragment placeholder.
ui._doc_bottom_cap: BottomNavigationView hard-caps at 5 items (Material design rule, enforced by NavigationBarMenu.addInternal → IllegalArgumentException). Sections with bottom_nav=false appear ONLY in the drawer; secondary / ops-y sections live there. Drive does the same: 4 in the bottom bar, the rest are drawer overflow.
ui._doc_home_index: The `home` section is the master index — its content is a TileGrid of every other section. Lives at the center of the bottom nav (replacing Chat, which moves to drawer-only). Tapping any drawer tab or bottom-nav button always lands the right-pane on that section's TileGrid (sub-pages as squared tiles).
ui._doc_aggregator_sections: Aggregator sections are pure NAV — their `tiles` deep-link into real content sections via target ids ('section:X' | 'page:X/Y' | 'action:X'). Each aggregator can declare tiles_shared (same in both modes), tiles_apps (front-end mode), and tiles_admin (back-end mode). The Apps/Admin global toggle (ModePrefs in MainActivity) picks which set renders. The bottom nav hosts exactly these 5 aggregators today: Communication · Infos · HOME · Suite · Tools.

sections._doc_icons: Per-mode icons: in Apps mode shows the everyday logs glyph; in Admin mode swaps to the C3-workflows glyph so the ops view reads as the workflows dashboard. Both the bottom-nav item AND the home_groups tile resolve via Section.iconForMode(mode) — single source of truth.

sections._doc_footers: Centered 'More' affordance rendered below the LAST group on each Suite surface. section_footer → Suite/Cloud (GroupedTilesFragment, below 'Tools Dashboards'); phone_footer → Suite/Phone (SuitePhoneAppsFragment, below 'Configs'). Each is a tile {id,label,icon,target} dispatched through the same onTileClicked grammar as any tile. Targets jump to the full Home Apps drawer: action:open_home_apps lands on the Cloud tab; action:open_home_apps_phone lands on the Phone tab.
sections._doc_phone_app_groups: Curated phone apps surfaced in Suite/Phone, grouped under the same titled sections used by Suite/Cloud (AI · Data Primary · Data Apps · Tools Primary · Tools Dashboards · Configs). Group order = render order. Each group renders as a subhead + UI_PHONE_GRID_COLUMNS-col grid (6 by default). Missing packages silently hidden — editing this list never breaks the render. Add a new group = add an object here; add an app to an existing group = append to its packages array.

phone_app_groups.title: AI
phone_app_groups._doc_folders: Nested folders inside a phone_app_group — render as One-UI-style folder tiles in the same grid as plain packages (2×2 mini-icon preview, tap → modal dialog with the contents at 5 cols). Empty folders silently skipped. SuitePhoneAppsFragment is the renderer.

sections._doc_tile_groups: Themed sub-groups for the Suite. tile_groups is the canonical schema, read by three surfaces: (1) bottom-nav Suite SECTION page → GroupedTilesFragment renders one titled row per group; (2) Home Apps Suite card → flattens all groups into a single horizontal scroll strip (home_groups entry has no group_explode); (3) aggregatorTilesFor flat fallback if anything else asks. Single source of truth — edit here, all surfaces update.

tiles.label: Chat-Matrix
tiles._doc: Routes to the Cloud-Comms constellation (matrix fork → hub → install Cloud-Comms-Hub.apk), same extapp mechanism as the Comms bottom-nav section and the Suite/AI IDE tile. Replaces the old app://im.vector.app launcher.

Browser uses ic_world (globe) so it's visually distinct from the Tabs tile (which keeps ic_mode_apps). target=page:browser/all lands the user directly on BrowserHostFragment's GRID instead of the section's page menu.

tiles._doc: App Tabs — surfaces the last 6 opened SuperApp sections / pages / external apps. Labeled 'Tabs' (the namespace freed by the Tabs→Browser rename). target=page:apptabs/grid so a tap goes STRAIGHT to AppTabsFragment; without this the section's single 'grid' page would still get wrapped in a page-menu intermediate.

tiles._doc: Native MyMaps section — foreground GPS tracker + MapLibre map + Timeline / Stops / Export pages. Was an external Google Maps deep-link until the in-app section landed in Push 2-3; tile now routes through SectionPages dispatch to the native fragments. For the system Google Maps launcher use action:app://com.google.android.apps.maps from anywhere else.

tiles._doc: Native MyFin section — beta dashboard rendered from ui.myfin_mock. Was an external GitHub Pages link until libs:fin landed; tile now routes through SectionPages dispatch → MyFinDashboardFragment.

tiles._doc: Native MyTrips section — Dashboard + Stats layered on top of MyMaps's local SQLite Stop store. Was an external GitHub Pages link until the in-app section landed in Push 2-3; tile now routes through SectionPages dispatch to the native Compose-less fragments (MytripsDashboardFragment / MytripsStatsFragment).

sections._doc_icons: Per-mode icons: Apps mode = multi-tools glyph (mymovies / mymusic / etc.); Admin mode = C3-stack glyph (infra dashboard read). Both the bottom-nav item AND the home_groups tile resolve via Section.iconForMode(mode).
sections._doc_label: Bottom-nav button displays 'Labs'. Section id stays 'tools' so deep-link grammar (page:tools/* / section:tools) and historical wiring don't break — this is a pure display rename.
sections._doc_tiles_shared: Master Lab index — 6 icon tiles, one per Lab. Read by the Home Apps Labs card (single flat strip via tiles_from_section) AND by aggregatorTilesFor as the canonical Labs roster. Each tile's target opens the Lab's stack page (page:tools/<lab-id>) — placeholder content until per-Lab stack is populated. Bottom-nav Labs still renders the linktree stack (stack_apps wins) so this list is the Home Apps face only.
sections._doc_pages: Per-Lab stack pages. Initially empty content (PageContentFragment fallback renders a stub) — wire each one to its dedicated content fragment as Labs come online.
sections.label: Labs
sections._doc_stack_apps: Labs/Apps tab — themed placeholder panels (Data & ML, Engineering, Quant & Markets, Aero & Space, Circus). kind=link_grid with empty links renders the title as a collapsable header until per-section content lands. Suite was removed (the Suite slide now lives only on the bottom-nav Suite section, not here).

sections.label: Mail
sections._doc_pages: Mapping to FairEmail's ~38 user-visible pages. Level-1 chips host the daily-use surfaces; Settings drills into 11 FairEmail FragmentOptions* sub-tabs; More is the overflow for rarely-used / diagnostic pages. Order: Folders first (operational entry point), then Inbox, then management (Accounts hosts the JMAP login form), then settings & overflow.

pages.label: Accounts
pages._doc: Hosts the JMAP login form (server/email/password) — Slice A landing surface. Moved here from the section index per the data-driven nav contract: the section's bottom-nav tap shows a TileGrid; account config is a sub-page, not the index.

sections._doc: RSS / ntfy lives in the drawer only now — Drive took its bottom-nav slot.

sections._doc: Master index — content is a TileGrid of every other section. Sits at the center of the bottom nav. No own drawer page (the [Home] drawer tab already covers it).

sections.label: Drive
sections._doc: Unified file storage hub — fronts filebrowser, photoprism, hedgedoc uploads, etherpad pads, borg/bup backup snapshots PLUS external cloud connections (S3 / Google Drive / Workspace / rclone remotes). Replaces RSS in the bottom-nav.

App Tabs — LRU shelf of the last 6 SuperApp things the user touched. Mix of section-level entries, page drill-downs, and external apps launched from the Phone tab. Single page 'grid' so the tile target page:apptabs/grid lands on AppTabsFragment.

sections._doc_rename: Renamed Tabs → Browser (and the underlying libs:browser module) so the 'Tabs' name space is free for the App Tabs feature (last-6 opened pages/apps). All section ids, deep-links, package names, and class names migrated; SharedPreferences file name 'tabs' kept so users' existing open-browser-tabs list survives the rename. Section icon = ic_world (globe) to visually distinguish from the App Tabs section which keeps ic_mode_apps.
sections.label: Browser

sections._doc: MyMaps — native GPS tracker + MapLibre map. Foreground-service LocationTrackerService writes points into a local SQLite DB; stop-detector emits Stop rows (centroid + min-dwell). Pages: map (MapLibre Native view), timeline (Daily | Stops tabs), configs (folds Tracker control + provider picker + API keys + calibration + Export buttons into one page). Export was a separate page until merged into Configs alongside Tracker — every Maps knob lives in one scroll now.
sections.label: MyMaps

sections._doc: MyTrips — dashboard layered on top of MyMaps's local SQLite tracker DB. Reads stops + points to render a daily-city-per-day list + 5-year rollup stats + heatmap. Push 3 fills this in; Push 2 ships a placeholder.

sections._doc: MyFin — personal finance dashboard (beta). Reads from build.json::ui.myfin_mock until a real aggregator lands. MyFinDashboardFragment in libs:fin reads UI_MYFIN_MOCK_B64 from BuildConfig (data-driven — edit JSON, rebuild, see new numbers).
sections.label: MyFin

sections._doc: In-app Wallet — first Jetpack Compose surface. Renders cards in a stack-overlap deck (Apple Wallet-style). Data layer = WalletStore in libs:core; SharedPreferences-backed; seeded with mock cards on first launch. Single page 'cards' so the tile target page:wallet/cards routes through the standard openSectionPage → SectionPages factory dispatcher (which knows about WalletFragment) instead of the bare-section placeholder.
sections.label: Wallet

sections._doc: MyHealth — native Health Connect dashboard. Reads the aggregated record set Garmin Connect / Google Fit / Samsung Health / Fitbit / Oura all sync into via androidx.health.connect:connect-client (one SDK = union of every source on-device). LOCAL-ONLY: HealthStore (libs:core, SharedPreferences) caches rollups, write-rate stats, source-app breakdowns, and last-sync timestamps. ZERO network calls — no OAuth, no webhooks, no cloud ingester.
sections._doc_pages: Three first-class pages: Summary (per-metric drill-in with 7d + 30d average tables), Timeline (date-picker → that day's per-metric values), Configs (Sources / Permissions / Stats / Raw / About sub-tabs + per-metric source toggles). Per-metric drill-down lives INSIDE each top-level page as Compose state — the section's drawer menu shows 3 entries, not 15.
sections._doc_metrics: Data-driven metric taxonomy — read by SummaryPage / TimelinePage / ConfigsPage to render the per-metric tiles + drill-downs. Each metric maps to one-or-more Health Connect record types via `records` (matched at runtime by class simple-name) + the perm subset via `perm_keys`. Add a metric = one entry here + tile icon. Removing a metric here removes it from all 3 top-level pages.
sections.label: MyHealth
sections._doc_taxonomy: Metric grouping mirrors Health Connect's own UI categories (verified against es-ES locale: Actividad / Constantes vitales / Medidas corporales / Nutrición / Seguimiento del ciclo / Sueño) so the per-metric counts in MyHealth match exactly what the HC permission screen shows. Vo2Max sits under Activity (not Heart) per HC; Exercise stays under Activity (no separate Workouts category in HC). Total perms across all metrics = 34, matching HC's count when every category is granted.

sections.label: Configs
sections._doc_pages_order: Order here is the single source of truth — drives both the Configs section page-grid AND (via home_groups tiles_from_section: 'config') the Home Apps Configs row. WireGuard appears in the row via an explicit `tiles` entry on the home_groups row with insert_after_id, since WG lives in its own section.

ui._doc_launcher_themes: Themes the user can pick in Configs → Launcher. The chosen theme drives MainActivity's home-pane chrome ONLY when the SuperApp is set as the Android Home / Launcher replacement. id maps to LauncherTheme enum; `default: true` marks the first-run choice. The `features` map on each theme is the DECLARATIVE contract Kotlin (Push B) will read to enable/disable chrome elements + background services. Adding a feature toggle = adding a key here; nothing in code needs to know the toggle name ahead of time. Cloud Theme = existing UI (Home3D + bottom nav + dynamic island). Cloud Minimalist Black = terminal aesthetic. Cloud Power Saving = battery-first; mirrors Samsung / Apple / Pixel power-save behaviour (no chrome, no animations, background paused) but keeps WireGuard tunnel ON so network connectivity stays alive — the SuperApp can't fall back to a stock Samsung power-saving picker because Samsung's classifier filters out home-launchers entirely (verified: even Samsung's app-search excludes us). Owning the mode is the only path.

launcher_themes.label: Cloud Theme
launcher_themes.subtitle: The default rich SuperApp UI — bottom nav, dynamic island, 3D home. Top status strip trimmed to Time · Battery only.

launcher_themes.label: Cloud Minimalist Black
launcher_themes.subtitle: Terminal aesthetic — pure black background, monospace green app list, no chrome. One-screen scroll.

launcher_themes.label: Cloud Power Saving
launcher_themes.subtitle: Battery-first launcher — dim OLED-black UI, no animations, no dynamic island, no 3D home. Background services paused EXCEPT WireGuard (network connectivity stays on). Mirrors Samsung / Apple / Pixel power-saving behaviour.

ui._doc_launcher_profiles: Profiles the user can pick in Configs → Launcher → Profiles. The chosen profile is persisted via LauncherProfilePrefs. Unlike themes (which control UI/chrome/features), profiles control APP ISOLATION + DATA SAFETY — which apps the user can reach and which subsystems get neutered (e.g. Guest disables WireGuard so the guest can't see private infra). The `behavior` map is the declarative contract Push C reads. Personal = full access (passthrough). Work = same as Personal for now; tag-based filtering wires in once apps carry app_tags. Guest = hands-off lockdown.

launcher_profiles.label: Personal
launcher_profiles.subtitle: Your default everyday profile — every installed app and folder visible.

launcher_profiles.label: Work
launcher_profiles.subtitle: Same as Personal for now — tag-based hide rules ship once each app/tile carries an app_tags list (e.g. work / personal / finance).

launcher_profiles.label: Guest
launcher_profiles.subtitle: Locked down — only the system browser is reachable. WireGuard tunnel disabled so the guest can't see your private mesh. No SuperApp sections, no chat, no mail, no vault.

ui._doc_maps_providers: Available geocoding providers. The user picks one per slot in Configs → Maps (kind: 'reverse' = city/neighborhood, 'poi' = restaurant/shop). 'host': 'free-noauth' = public free endpoint, no account, fair-use rate limit; 'free-account' = free tier behind signup; 'paid' = billing required; 'self' = our own deployment at endpoint URL. requires_api_key=true means we look up the key in MapsApiKeyPrefs. New providers: add a JSON entry + supply the key (if any) in Configs → Maps → API Keys; no Kotlin edits.
ui._doc_maps_active: Default-selected provider per slot at first launch. User changes them at runtime in Configs → Maps (persisted in MapsProviderPrefs). Defaults are free-noauth = zero account / zero key — works out of the box on a fresh install.
ui._doc_maps_tracking: Tracker calibration — first-run defaults for the foreground GPS service. User tunes via Configs → Maps → Calibration sliders, persisted in MapsTrackingPrefs. `interval_moving_ms` = GPS poll cadence when speed > moving_threshold_mps. `interval_stopped_ms` = poll cadence when below threshold. `stops_radius_m` + `stops_dwell_min` = the Stop detector: must dwell within radius for at least dwell_min minutes to register a Stop event (the only event that fires a reverse-geocode + POI lookup — the 'batching trick').
ui._doc_myfin_mock: MyFin beta dashboard data — fully editable here, baked into libs:fin's BuildConfig at gradle config time so MyFinDashboardFragment reads it via BuildConfig.UI_MYFIN_MOCK_B64. Currency strings are display-only (the fragment just prints what's here); flip to a real aggregator by swapping the loader, not by replacing this block. Numbers are illustrative.
ui._doc_dynamic_island_action: What happens when the user taps the dynamic-island pill in the toolbar. Format: `app:<packageName>` opens that app's launcher activity, `notifications` opens the Notification Centre (legacy default), `shortcut:<id>` fires one of MainActivity's shortcut intents. Falls back to a silent Toast if the target app isn't installed — does NOT silently re-open notifications, to keep the user's explicit binding the source of truth.
ui._doc_home_apps_tabs: Tabs at the top of the Home Apps swipe-up sheet (AppDrawerSheetFragment). Cloud = the existing HomeGroupedFragment (cloud-service tile grid derived from home_groups). Phone = PhoneAppsFragment (Android-launcher folder grid of installed apps grouped by phone_folders). Order = display order.
ui._doc_phone_grid_columns: Column count for the Phone tab's folder grid. Mirrors tile_columns (6) so the two tabs share the same density rhythm.
ui._doc_phone_folders: Folder taxonomy for the Phone tab — categorised by function (main purpose of the app), not by manufacturer. The `label` keeps the user's prefix sort markers verbatim (_#, _, -, .#, .a, .b, >) so the order reads identically to native One UI. `order` is the lexicographic sort key (two-digit blocks let new folders slot between existing ones). `match_keywords` are case-insensitive matches against the app's `packageName` and `label`. Five syntaxes (PhoneAppClassifier.matches): (1) `pkg:com.foo.bar` = exact packageName; (2) `pkg^com.foo.` = packageName.startsWith; (3) `lbl:Exact Label` = label exact; (4) `lbl~substring` = label contains (min 3 chars); (5) plain string = legacy substring on `pkg + label` (REQUIRES min length 4 to suppress catastrophic false-positives like `bb` matching `bbva` AND every package containing the letters `bb` anywhere). First matching folder wins, first matching keyword inside a folder wins. PREFER `pkg:` for known installed apps — it's the only form that can't false-match. TWO distinct sinks, different roles: (a) `_New Apps` (id=new_apps, order=98, empty keywords) is the AUTOMATIC sink — anything our keyword list doesn't know yet lands here, signal to the user that a new app needs triage / a new keyword / a new folder; (b) `_Misc` (id=misc, order=99) is the MANUAL sink — give it specific keywords to deliberately push hand-picked apps there. New Apps shrinks as keywords improve; Misc only grows when the user adds something to it on purpose. Manufacturer (Google / Samsung / non-Play-Store) is metadata for Smart Folders (see phone_smart_folders below) — NOT a primary grouping criterion.
ui._doc_phone_sections: Top-level section headers in the Home Apps/Phone tab. Folders are bucketed under a section by their label's first character: System (_), Services (-), Tools A (.), Tools B (>). Order = render order. Empty sections (every folder empty) silently skipped. Phone tab renders one subhead per non-empty section + the folder grid below.
ui._doc_phone_smart_folders: Smart Folders rendered at the BOTTOM of the Home Apps/Phone tab — dynamic filters over the same LauncherApps.getActivityList enumeration the page uses. Apps still belong to their topical folder above; Smart Folders are an orthogonal cross-cut view by manufacturer / install-source. Rule types: pkg_prefix (any pkg starts-with one of values); pkg_eq (any pkg equals one of values); install_source_in (the app's install-source-of-record — installingPackageName OR initiatingPackageName from PackageManager.getInstallSourceInfo — IS one of values; use this to bucket apps by the store/installer that owns their updates); install_source_not (install source NOT in values — legacy catch-all for 'anything outside the official stores'); recently_installed (ranking rule: newest firstInstallTime first, capped at `limit`). The install-source values are real installer package names — verified on-device via /api/phone/classify (which dumps installing/initiating/system per app): com.android.vending=Google Play, com.sec.android.app.samsungapps=Galaxy Store, com.uptodown=Uptodown, org.fdroid.fdroid=F-Droid, com.google.android.packageinstaller=manual sideload (raw APK, no store), com.epicgames.portal=Epic, com.facebook.system=Meta's own installer.

ui._doc_wireguard_default: Seeds the Configs/WireGuard form on first run. The phone is a mesh spoke; defaults point at the gcp-proxy hub (mesh.json::nodes[0]). Peers is an array so the user can talk to multiple mesh nodes in parallel — first-run we seed only gcp-proxy; in-app the user can Add Peer / Remove Peer to grow or shrink the list. User-editable at runtime via WireGuardFragment (persisted in WireGuardPrefs SharedPreferences); these values are only the FIRST-RUN defaults. interface_private_key, peer.public_key, peer.preshared_key are NOT seeded — generate via the in-app Generate Keypair button, import via a .conf file, or paste manually.
ui._doc_modes: Global UI mode toggle (Apps ↔ Admin). Lives in the toolbar (top-right). Aggregator sections render tiles_apps OR tiles_admin based on currentMode; sections with tiles_shared ignore the mode. Persisted via ModePrefs (regular SharedPreferences — not encrypted, it's just a view-pref).
ui._doc_home_actions: App-level action tiles shown in the Home master TileGrid AFTER the section tiles. Each `action_type` is handled by MainActivity.onTileClicked('action:<id>'). A URL-shaped action_type is launched via launchUri. Extend by adding entries here — never hardcoded in Kotlin.
ui._doc_home_drawer_prepend: Drawer menu entries prepended ABOVE the first section. Same {label, icon, action_type} shape as home_actions; dispatched through MainActivity.dispatchHomeAction. Use for quick-access items that aren't tied to a single section — e.g. opening the swipe-up Home Apps sheet from the drawer too.

ui._doc_home_groups: Home master view is organised into themed groups (Home / Comms / Infos / Suite / Labs / Configs). The first group 'Home' is a meta-row whose tiles deep-link to the OTHER groups' parent sections — call it a master index. Each tile's `id` is 'section:<X>' (switch section) or 'page:<section>/<page>' (deep-link), rendered tile_columns-per-row by HomeGroupedFragment. Both Suite and Labs entries FLATTEN their referenced section's tiles into a single horizontal-scroll strip — Suite pulls sections[suite].tile_groups (all 18 tiles), Labs pulls sections[tools].tiles_shared (6 Lab icons, each opening page:tools/<lab-id>). Single source of truth — change this to reshape the Home page, nothing else.

home_groups._doc: Home Apps Suite — FLATTENED card. tiles_from_section pulls sections[suite].tile_groups and flattens them in declaration order into a single horizontal-scroll strip (group_explode is OFF / absent). The grouped layout still lives on the bottom-nav Suite SECTION page via GroupedTilesFragment, so the sub-titles aren't lost — they're just absent from Home Apps. scroll=horizontal so all 18 tiles ride one strip; per-tile smooth scroll, not snap-per-page.

home_groups._doc: Home Apps Labs — ONE card containing 6 icon tiles (master Lab index). tiles_from_section flattens sections[tools].tiles_shared into this card (no group_explode). Each icon → page:tools/<lab-id> opens that Lab's stack page (placeholder content for now). scroll=horizontal so the 6 icons ride a single strip and stay reachable without wrapping into multiple rows.

ui._doc_external_apps: Companion Android apps the SuperApp launches instead of rendering an in-app fragment. A tile target of `extapp:<id>/<fork_key>` (see ui.sections[communication]) resolves here: MainActivity.launchExternalApp tries the per-fork package, then the hub package, then — if neither is installed — hands install_apk_url + install_package to libs:updater (PackageInstaller prompt). Fully data-driven: package ids + the GitHub-release APK URL live ONLY here, never in Kotlin. Cloud-Comms = the constellation hub (com.diegonmarcos.comms) + 3 fork APKs; appIds mirror ea_cloud-comms/build.json::forks[*].app_id, the install URL mirrors its release.gh_release (rolling `latest` asset Cloud-Comms-Hub.apk).
ui._doc_kde_connect: KDE Connect integration config consumed by libs:kde-connect (Configs > KDE page). SELF-CONTAINED — does NOT launch the installed org.kde.kdeconnect_tp. KDE Connect discovery is UDP broadcast on the LAN, which does NOT cross WireGuard; and the peer answers to the packet's SOURCE IP, so the packet must leave over wg0. For each device we declare its wg_ip; libs:kde-connect binds its probe + identity socket to the native VPN (wg0) Network and tries that FIRST (so the source IP is the wg0 address the Surface can route back to), then the default route, then a self-contained LAN broadcast. `package` is retained as metadata for the future vendor phase, not launched. wg_ip values mirror data/mesh.json (Surface Pro = node 'laptop' = 10.0.0.5). Add a device = append here; nothing in Kotlin hardcodes an IP.

deploy.note: APK produced in dist/. Side-loadable via adb or shared via Filebrowser.

release._doc: Data-driven publish targets for the APK. build.sh oras-push + build.sh gh-release read this block; the GHA workflow (1_workflows/src/cicd/ship-cloud-superapp.yml) invokes those engine commands — no hardcoded registry/tag strings in the workflow.

artifact._doc: Path under dist/ to publish. The `debug` key is the daily-driver build (no ProGuard, real stacktraces, debug keystore) — it is THE app for this stack, not a side-by-side dev variant. The `release` key exists for when a true Play-Store-style release lifecycle lands; the GHA workflow picks debug for main pushes.

ghcr._doc: ORAS push as an OCI artifact (not a container — APK is a blob). One :latest tag plus per-commit sha + per-version tags. Image renamed from `superapp` to `cloud-superapp` — old package becomes orphan.

gh_release._doc: GitHub Release attachment. rolling_tag is the canonical mode now: one release named (default `latest`) the ship workflow overwrites on every main push, so the linktree Android download link stays stable. tag_pattern stays as legacy for immutable per-tag releases when invoked under a tag push context (rolling release still publishes alongside).

phone_install._doc: Targets for build.sh phone-install. Pulls APK from GHCR via curl+OCI HTTP API (no oras dep — works on aarch64 Termux without a Nix shell) and copies to a target dir an Android file manager can see. Override target_dir per environment via PHONE_TARGET env var; default suits Termux/nix-on-droid where ~/storage symlinks to /storage/emulated/0/.

auto_update._doc: In-app updater config — read at gradle eval time into BuildConfig, then used by libs:updater at runtime. Same registry/namespace/image as release.ghcr (the engine asserts consistency at build time).
auto_update._doc_interval: WorkManager periodic minimum is 15 min. 6h matches typical update cadence + spares battery / data.
auto_update._doc_install: Behavior when an update is available: 'prompt' uses PackageInstaller with a foreground notification — user must accept install per Android security model. 'silent' requires the system updater privilege which only F-Droid Privileged Extension can grant.
